title: Second Bengal Biennale, 'Banalata', opens in Santiniketan on 25 November and Kolkata on 28 November
dek: The multi-venue art biennale returns for a second edition, curated by the Chander Haat collective and Ritika Biswas around Jibanananda Das's poem Banalata Sen. It runs until 2 January 2027.
body: The Bengal Biennale, first held in 2024, returns for its second edition under the title Banalata. It opens in Santiniketan on 25 November 2026 and in Kolkata on 28 November, and runs until 2 January 2027, according to the festival listings and later reports. An early announcement carried by PTI on 8 October had given 15 November as the start; reports since then all give 25 November.

The organiser is the Gameplan Foundation, whose trustees are Jeet and Malavika Banerjee. The curators are Chander Haat, an artist collective that works on community-based projects in Sarsuna in south Kolkata, and Ritika Biswas, an independent curator and researcher.

The title comes from Jibanananda Das's 1942 poem Banalata Sen and from the Bangla word for a wild forest vine. According to the PTI report, the curators use it to explore ecology, buried histories and the cultural geography of Bengal, holding poetry and politics together.

Venues named in the PTI report include, in Santiniketan, the Nandan Art Museum and Gallery, the Santiniketan Society of Visual Art and Design, Arthshila and the Somnath Hore Studio; and in Kolkata, the Alipore Museum (a former jail), the Indian Museum, the Lalit Kala Akademi and the Kolkata Centre for Creativity. Homegrown also lists the Victoria Memorial among the Kolkata venues.
Artists named so far include Arpita Singh, Atul Dodiya, Ayoung Kim, Ashfika Rahman and the Britto Arts Trust. The full programme had not been published when the reports appeared.
